segments.t: When Vika smells alcohol behind the bar and asks Kostya if he broke a bottle, Kostya turns to Max to back up his alibi. Refusing to break his promise of honesty, Max tells Vika the truth, which finally convinces her to let him help with the crib.
Ты что-то разбил?
Я? Нет, я ничего не разбивал.
Этого вообще никто не видел. Правда, Макс?
Костян, извини. Я обещал Вике не врать.
Это неправда.
Там был коньяк, и он дешёвый был.
Вик, слушай, я правда изменился.
Давай я тебе помогу, а?
Ладно.
Здорово! Я тогда быстро переодеться сбегаю.
Пять минут, и никуда не уходи, ладно?
Эй, ты кто такой?
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Ты что-то разбил?
'Did you break something?' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'broke' places the action in the masculine past tense.
Я? Нет, я ничего не разбивал.
'Me? No, I did not break anything.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'broke' without extra filler words.
Этого вообще никто не видел. Правда, Макс?
'Nobody saw a thing at all. Right, Max?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'this' before landing on 'Max'.
Костян, извини. Я обещал Вике не врать.
'Kostyan, sorry. I promised Vika not to lie.' In Russian, the idea of 'Kostyan' flows naturally into 'to lie' without extra filler words.
Это неправда.
'That is not true.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'this' before landing on 'untrue'.
Там был коньяк, и он дешёвый был.
'There was cognac there, and it was cheap.' In Russian, the idea of 'there' flows naturally into 'cheap' without extra filler words.
Вик, слушай, я правда изменился.
'Vika, listen, I really have changed.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'Vika' and finishing on 'have changed'.
Давай я тебе помогу, а?
'Let me help you, huh?' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'and' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
Ладно.
'Alright.' The meaning hinges on 'all right' working together with 'all right' in spoken Russian.
Здорово! Я тогда быстро переодеться сбегаю.
'Great! Then I will quickly run to change clothes.' The grammar packs 'great' and 'will run over' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Пять минут, и никуда не уходи, ладно?
'Five minutes, and do not go anywhere, okay?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'five' and finishing on 'all right'.
Эй, ты кто такой?
'Hey, who are you?' In Russian, the idea of 'hey' flows naturally into 'such' without extra filler words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

And that concludes the dining room exchange. Listen for how Max apologizes to Kostya because he promised Vika not to lie, and then spots an intruder in the locker room. See you in the next scene.
